grammar.title: 第 for ordinal numbers
grammar.explanation: 第 (dì) turns a plain number into an ordinal: 第二 ("second"), 第一 ("first"). Compare 两个 ("two [things]") with 第二个 ("the second [thing]") — the meaning changes completely once 第 is added.

grammar.title: 常/常常 for "often"
grammar.explanation: 常 (cháng) means "often", and doubling it to 常常 (chángcháng) makes the same meaning a little more emphatic and conversational. Both go directly before the verb, just like other frequency adverbs such as 也 and 都.

grammar.title: 一点儿 for "a little"
grammar.explanation: 一点儿 (yìdiǎnr) means "a little" or "a bit". After an adjective, it softens a comparison or request: 慢一点儿 ("a little slower"), 大一点儿 ("a bit bigger"). After a verb like 要 or 会, it just means a small amount.

sentences.pinyin: Zhè shì dì èr gè, bú shì liǎng gè.
sentences.en: This is the second one, not two of them.
This one is a bit bigger.
